page.notes: Running head and page number read as printed; the page number "182" is slightly blurred. Woodcut initial at the start of the epigraph is an ornamental O (the letter is joined to "Ornicatio"); the O is partly hidden, so the initial letter is uncertain. "Efd." is printed this way; the abbreviation may be Esd. or Eccl., so it is marked [?]. "Ia" in the black-letter line is uncertain. Black-letter German passages are marked with bl. The catchword "vitiis" stands alone at the right below the last line. Hyphenated line-end words: "gau-dia", "de-trimentosam", "mu-stum", "consul-tat", "fecit(e-um)", "Ec-cles.".
